reference: No matching GNU/POSIX CLI implements this in-memory terminal-model API. Contract outputs are independently derived from the documented Bash builtin interface, ECMA-48/DEC cursor and DSR behavior, OSC 0/2 title behavior, and xterm 256-color/truecolor SGR encodings. No expected output is taken from the candidate.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata reports vt as a builtin and exposes its help.
Grid dimensions, initial cursor coordinates, cursor addressing, text rendering, and resize clamping.
OSC 0/2 window-title storage and the DSR cursor-position reply buffer.
DEC private-mode enable/disable reporting and indexed, grayscale, truecolor, and reset SGR helpers.
exclusions: No matching standalone GNU command exists, so runnable cases are honest API contract checks rather than GNU parity comparisons.
Full xterm/VT100 parser conformance needs a separately pinned terminal reference transcript corpus.
PTY client integration and terminal resize/input behavior need an isolated PTY driver and disposable VM; they are deferred below.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash classifies vt as a loadable builtin through the type metadata interface.
Confirm Bash help can resolve the documented vt command surface without invoking a terminal operation.
cases.script:
help vt > metadata.out
printf 'vt help available\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented ROWS COLS size output and 1-indexed initial cursor on a small grid.
cases.script:
vt new -h v -W 4 -H 2
vt size "$v"
vt cursor "$v"
vt free "$v"

cases.purpose: Verify printable characters and ECMA-48 CUP addressing, then check the documented text rendering of the occupied cells.
cases.script:
vt new -h v -W 6 -H 2
vt feed "$v" $'A\e[2;3HZ'
vt cursor "$v"
vt render "$v"
vt free "$v"

cases.purpose: Check the documented resize behavior: dimensions change and a cursor outside the new grid is clamped to its final row and column.
cases.script:
vt new -h v -W 8 -H 4
vt feed "$v" $'\e[4;8H'
vt resize "$v" -W 5 -H 2
vt size "$v"
vt cursor "$v"
vt free "$v"

cases.purpose: Check that the documented OSC 0 and OSC 2 title sequences can set and retrieve the window title.
cases.script:
vt new -h v -W 8 -H 2
vt feed "$v" $'\e]2;fixture title\a'
vt title "$v"
vt feed "$v" $'\e]0;second title\e\\'
vt title "$v"
vt free "$v"

cases.purpose: Verify ECMA-48 DSR 6 returns the 1-indexed current cursor position through the documented response-drain API.
cases.script:
vt new -h v -W 6 -H 2
vt feed "$v" $'\e[6n'
vt response "$v"
vt free "$v"

cases.purpose: Check DECSET/DECRST state for SGR mouse and bracketed paste, including the VT default autowrap mode documented by the API.
cases.script:
vt new -h v -W 8 -H 2
vt feed "$v" $'\e[?1006h\e[?2004h'
active=$(vt mode "$v")
[[ $active == *mouse-sgr* && $active == *bracketed-paste* && $active == *autowrap* ]]
vt feed "$v" $'\e[?1006l\e[?2004l'
[[ $(vt mode "$v") == autowrap ]]
printf 'DEC modes enabled and cleared\n'
vt free "$v"

cases.purpose: Check documented color helpers against independently computed xterm 256-color cube/grayscale indices, truecolor SGR, and SGR reset bytes.
cases.script:
vt color-cube 5 0 0 -V fg
vt color-bg-cube 0 5 5 -V bg
vt color-grayscale 0 -V gray0
vt color-bg-grayscale 23 -V gray23
vt color-rgb 1 2 255 -V rgb
vt color-reset -V reset
[[ $fg == $'\e[38;5;196m' && $bg == $'\e[48;5;51m' && $gray0 == $'\e[38;5;232m' && $gray23 == $'\e[48;5;255m' && $rgb == $'\e[38;2;1;2;255m' && $reset == $'\e[0m' ]]
printf 'SGR encodings match\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise vt with a client connected to a pseudo-terminal, including terminal input forwarding and resize events.
Compare broader parser behavior across VT100/xterm control-sequence classes against an independent terminal implementation.
A cursor-addressing sequence split across feed calls retains parser state and places a single printable cell.
cases.script:
vt new -h v -W 6 -H 3
vt feed "$v" $'\e[2;'
vt feed "$v" '3HZ'
vt cursor "$v"
vt render "$v"
vt free "$v"

cases.purpose: DSR reflects the addressed cursor and the second response call emits no stale reply.
cases.script:
vt new -h v -W 6 -H 2
vt feed "$v" $'\e[2;3H\e[6n'
vt response "$v"
vt response "$v"
vt free "$v"
